target_customer: Real estate agents, plus insurance agents and loan officers per CB Insights, who need leads and booked appointments
problem: Agents spend time cold calling and following up with leads; Smart Alto qualified leads and set appointments for them.
business_model: B2B SaaS and services for real estate professionals; the current site sells property data and lead generation software with a free trial
product_category: Real estate lead qualification and property intelligence software

founders.name: Hassan Riggs
founders.background_notes: YC page: former inside sales agent and digital marketer who says he sold over 100 million dollars in products. Education from the YC page.

founders.name: Wayne Anderson
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as cofounder and COO with no bio.

investors: Google for Startups Black Founders Fund

technical_complexity.rationale: Lead response and appointment setting by texting and calling is standard software plus operations for an eight person team.

defensibility.rationale: No source shows data or integration lock in at the time; lead response tools were copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows copying by incumbents. The company later moved toward property data and lead generation software, per its site.

market_need_then: Agents' cold calling and lead follow up burden is the stated pain in the Hypepotamus profile title and the YC page; no dated quantified demand source was found.

branding.domain_note: Uses smartalto.com, a descriptive compound domain.
branding.community_and_virality: Local Birmingham press (Alabama News Center 2023, Hypepotamus, Business Alabama 2022) covers the company and CEO, but not the brand itself.

brand_strength.rationale: The name suggests intelligence and a smart assistant but is generic (smart prefix), and press focused on the founder and Alabama story rather than the brand.

pivots.from: Appointment setting and lead qualification for real estate agents
pivots.to: Property intelligence and lead generation software with AI enrichment
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from the company website product description, undated

outcome_analysis: Smart Alto went through YC Winter 2017, moved operations to Birmingham, Alabama, and appeared to keep operating: it received a 100 thousand dollar Google Black Founders Fund award in 2022 and its website was live with a 2024 footer. YC lists it Inactive and the CEO as a former founder, which conflicts with the live site, and no shutdown or acquisition was found. No failure cause is public and no clear success story is documented, so factors are left empty.
notes: The 2017-03 seed rests on a single database (Seedtable) with no amount; CB Insights reports 440K raised over 6 rounds and another aggregator reports 1.0M or 1.1M, so rounds are missing. The Google grant is non dilutive and the date is from a September 2022 local report and an August 2022 Google blog. Alabama News Center could not be fetched (rate limited). YC status Inactive conflicts with a live 2024 website, so exit is unknown. Founded year is given as 2016 or 2017 across sources so it is null. No dated competitor sources found, list empty. The YC page does not name employers for Riggs.
